hero.title: Cybersecurity Analyst.
hero.accent: A technical mindset. A security focus.
hero.intro: I’m Diogo Vidazinha, a SOC Analyst at Fujitsu. I work with security monitoring, alert investigation and threat intelligence, building on a background in Computer Engineering.
hero.note: Fujitsu SOC · Master’s student at IPBeja

about.title:
Engineering foundations.
A career in cyber defense.
about.lead: From systems and software to the analysis of security events, I bring an engineering approach to understanding how technology works — and how to protect it.
paragraphs: At Fujitsu’s Security Operations Center, my work includes alert triage, IOC analysis and blocking, SIEM monitoring with Splunk, and investigation of IP reputation. I value clear documentation and well-defined escalation workflows.

Alongside my SOC role, I am pursuing a Master’s in Cybersecurity Engineering and Cybercrime at IPBeja. My undergraduate studies in Computer Engineering are nearing completion, with the internship presentation still pending.
Balancing work and study since the age of 16, including more than five years of customer-facing experience, has strengthened my communication, time management and adaptability.

experience.title:
From infrastructure
to security operations.
experience.intro: Hands-on experience across enterprise security, systems and IT infrastructure.

items.summary: Security monitoring and investigation in an enterprise SOC, with a focus on triage, threat context and clear operational handover.
bullets: Monitor security events and investigate alerts using Splunk.
Triage, analyse and block indicators of compromise (IOCs).
Investigate threat intelligence and IP reputation with VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB and Spur.
Track incidents in Jira, document analysis and follow security escalation workflows.

items.summary: Curricular internship within Fujitsu Portugal’s Managed Detection and Response (MDR) service, supporting security monitoring, alert analysis and incident response, followed by a professional role in the SOC team.
Practical IT experience in a demanding industrial environment, including communications support more than 1,000 metres underground.
bullets: Worked with Active Directory, Group Policy and endpoint management using SCCM.
Gained hands-on experience with VMware, Veeam, networking and infrastructure support.
Used PowerShell for automation and supported day-to-day IT operations.

additional.summary: Over five years of customer-facing work alongside my studies, strengthening communication, responsibility and time management.
Connected the academic community with early-career talent initiatives, with a focus on communication and collaboration.

projects.title:
Ideas turned into
working systems.
projects.intro: Software, scientific computing and infrastructure work. Each project reflects a different part of my technical background.

items.name: BigData Helper
items.description: A web application that helps users choose a suitable Big Data architecture through a guided, rule-based decision process.
items.challenge: Translate architecture selection criteria into a multi-step questionnaire and a rule-based recommendation flow.
items.outcome: User authentication, project management, analysis history and architecture comparison in a single application.

items.name: Using artificial intelligence to support age-group classification of Netflix content
items.description: Scientific work on using artificial intelligence to support age-group classification of Netflix content.
items.challenge: Explore the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning to content age classification.
items.outcome: Preparation and online presentation of the article at CISTI 2026, co-authored with Denis Cicau.

items.name: Book Exchange
items.description: A book-exchange application with authentication, full CRUD operations and database integration.
items.challenge: Implement backend logic and a consistent desktop interface, connected to persistent data.
items.outcome: An application that brings authentication, data management and a JavaFX interface together.

items.name: Earth–Moon Simulation
items.description: A numerical model of the Earth–Moon–spacecraft three-body problem, exploring orbital sensitivity and chaotic behaviour.
items.challenge: Model multiple initial conditions using SciPy’s adaptive Runge–Kutta 5(4) solver.
items.outcome: Numerical analysis and visualisation of how initial conditions affect trajectories.

items.name: IT in an industrial environment
items.description: Systems, networking and communications work in a mining environment, documented in an internship report.
items.challenge: Support IT infrastructure and communications in demanding operational conditions.
items.outcome: Practical exposure to virtualisation, backup, endpoint management and infrastructure support.
